diffuseAlbedo.source: Palette.json accent.cotton-tulle: an undyed cotton net aged to ivory, as the bronzes' skirts are seen; no measured reflectance was read
diffuseAlbedo.note: Lighter than the silks, darker than new white cotton: a century's yellowing and dust.

refractiveIndex.source: South Coast Air Quality Management District, SCAQMD Method 317-93, Qualitative Analysis of Natural or Man-Made Fiber Types (approved May 1993, revised August 1996), Table 1 'Optical properties of natural fibers' (compiled from The Particle Atlas): cotton, length 1.578, cross 1.532, birefringence 0.046; https://www.aqmd.gov/docs/default-source/laboratory-procedures/methods-procedures/317-93.pdf
refractiveIndex.note: Checked against the PDF's Table 1; the values match. The row is native cotton. The same table gives mercerized cotton as length 1.544-1.566 and cross 1.522-1.524. If the net is mercerized, the average falls to about 1.53-1.54 and the lower bound to 1.522. Ageing and yellowing of the fibre are not covered.
refractiveIndex.derivation: Orientation average of a uniaxial fibre lying every way: (n_par + 2 n_perp)/3 = (1.578 + 2 x 1.532)/3 = 1.547; the simple mean of the two is 1.555. Both round to 1.55. min and max are the fibre's two principal indices.

porosity.note: A tulle is mostly its net's openings; a first share of void until an aged specimen is measured.

wettingDepth.note: A single layer of fine net's thickness.

grain.source: Corbet, M. (2013) 'Cotton Tulle - There's a Big Difference!', Needle 'n Thread, 20 Nov 2013, https://www.needlenthread.com/2013/11/cotton-tulle.html (cotton hexagon-net tulle at 18 hpi, hexagons per inch; a reader's comment reports English netting at 20 hexagons per inch); AllThreads, 'Tulle net', https://www.allthreads.com.au/products/tulle (100 % cotton hexagonal hole lace net, 14 holes per inch)
grain.note: Accepted with the source statement corrected. The 20-per-inch figure comes from a reader's comment under the article, not from the article, which gives only 18 hpi. The article describes a cotton machine-made hexagon net and states no fibre percentage. The count direction of 'per inch' in a bobbinet is not specified, so the pitch is approximate. The skirt's own net was not measured.
grain.derivation: mesh pitch = 25.4 mm / hexagons per inch: 25.4/18 = 1.41 mm; range 25.4/20 = 1.27 mm to 25.4/14 = 1.81 mm

bed.note: The gathers' folds at the waistband, the coarsest unevenness the skirt shows.

bedAspect.note: Gathers run down the skirt: how much longer than wide.

hurst.note: A first self-affinity for a net's unevenness, as the museum's silks take.

toneSpread.note: Uneven yellowing and dust across the layers.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range across the cloth.

roughness.note: Spun cotton's twisted staple fibres scatter broadly: far rougher than a filament silk's 0.3.

sheen.note: A staple yarn's standing fibre ends give a soft rim of sheen; a first weight.

sheenRoughness.note: A first spread of the sheen.
